newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-BHP wins waiver on oil drill reports.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-BHP wins waiver on oil drill reports.

text.p: The Australian Stock Exchange (ASX) said on Thursday it has granted a six-month waiver to The Broken Hill Pty Co Ltd from providing weekly drilling reports on the progress of wells which are outside Australian jurisdiction and in Timor Sea the zone of cooperation with Indonesia.
The ASX also said the waiver, which ends on April 23 next year, will apply to wells within Australian jurisdiction on a case-by-case basis.
BHP must, however, report significant events from all wells if the information is deemed to have a material effect on the company's share price.
The waiver applies to listing rules which require companies to provide weekly drilling reports showing depth of drilling, any hydrocarbon shows, and flow levels, among other things.

The ASX said one condition applying to its waiver was that the information about the drilling reports remain confidential to BHP and that it release the terms of the waiver to the market. It said the six month limit would allow the ASX to review the issues raised by BHP's application.
The ASX revealed on October 17 that it was in dispute with BHP about the company's weekly reports, traditionally issued each Thursday afternoon.

At the time, the ASX queried the amount of information provided about the Buffalo One exploration well in the Timor Sea. BHP said at the start of the month that the well was in the process of being plugged and abandoned but on October 14 said the well had flowed 11,790 barrels per day.
In its submission, BHP said the ASX listing rules dealing with weekly reports had no international equivalent and could mean that industry intelligence was issued to competitors.
BHP also said its partners had found the rules to be totally unacceptable and this potentially made BHP an undesirable joint venture partner. -- Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
